slice.leaf: Audit the OpenTimestamps public-calendar submission protocol for the minimum unauthenticated immediate timestamp-creation contract, retry/idempotency behavior, quota/cost properties, and scheduled-Chat transport fit without submitting anything.
slice.action: Public-primary-source protocol audit only; no timestamp submission, plugin installation/connection, protected/manual execution, scheduler mutation, O/downstream/other-worker semantic read, or external paid/quota-bearing compute was used.

sources.observation: Public calendar servers are described as free to use and requiring no registration or API key; default calendars are exposed for timestamp creation.

RemoteCalendar.submit constructs an HTTP request to <calendar>/digest with the raw digest as request body, headers Accept: application/vnd.opentimestamps.v1 and User-Agent, requires HTTP 200, reads at most 10000 response bytes, and deserializes the response as a Timestamp committing to the submitted digest. No authentication parameter or API key is part of this client contract.

POST /digest accepts Content-Length convertible to an integer from 0 through 64 inclusive, reads exactly that many raw bytes, submits them to the aggregator, and on success returns HTTP 200 application/octet-stream containing the serialized timestamp. Invalid length returns HTTP 400.

Aggregator.submit wraps each submitted message with nonce_timestamp before aggregation; nonce_timestamp uses a fresh 16-byte os.urandom nonce. JournalWriter appends commitments and fsyncs them. Therefore repeating the same digest is not byte-for-byte idempotent: each accepted retry can create a distinct pending proof/commitment path rather than recovering the first lost response.

minimum_submission_contract.path: /digest relative to an allowed public calendar base URL
minimum_submission_contract.request_body: raw digest bytes; server accepts 0..64 bytes, while the normal OTS file-hash path uses a cryptographic digest such as SHA-256
minimum_submission_contract.user_agent_observed: python-opentimestamps by default; not evidenced as authentication
minimum_submission_contract.authentication: none in the official client/public-calendar contract
minimum_submission_contract.success_body: serialized OpenTimestamps Timestamp committing to the submitted digest

retry_and_idempotency.same_digest_retry_semantics: NOT_IDEMPOTENT_BY_PROOF_BYTES_OR_SERVER_APPEND; a fresh nonce is generated per accepted submission, so a retry may create another valid independent pending timestamp path.
retry_and_idempotency.lost_response_recovery: No source-qualified endpoint was found that lets a client recover the first submission from only the original digest after losing its serialized response, because the server-side nonce is fresh and not derivable from the digest.
retry_and_idempotency.safe_client_rule: Treat submission as at-least-once. Persist any successful serialized proof before considering another attempt. If an earlier response is unknown, a later retry should be recorded as a new stamp attempt, not as idempotent replay or proof recovery. Do not same-run retry under RUN_LIFECYCLE.

candidate_assessment.expected_completion_time: low at protocol level: one small HTTP POST plus local proof persistence; blockchain completion remains asynchronous
candidate_assessment.success_probability: high for protocol simplicity but current scheduled-Chat transport availability is unproven
candidate_assessment.conflict_duplication_risk: medium: raw POST is simple, but retries can create duplicate independent proofs unless client-local idempotency state is enforced
candidate_assessment.integration_cost: low if an already-exposed arbitrary HTTPS binary POST transport exists; otherwise unresolved
candidate_assessment.finite_monthly_trial_paid_quota_dependen: NONE_REQUIRED_BY_DOCUMENTED_PUBLIC_CALENDAR_CONTRACT: official service states free use with no registration/API key. This does not prove unlimited availability or absence of operational rate limiting.
candidate_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_or_manual: UNRESOLVED_FOR_IMMEDIATE_CREATION because this scheduled-Chat run exposes no proven arbitrary HTTPS POST surface to the calendar endpoint.

slice.tested_scope: Only the public OpenTimestamps calendar HTTP submission contract and its source-visible retry/idempotency semantics were audited. No live calendar request was sent and no claim is made about current calendar uptime, hidden service limits, or a currently exposed Chat transport beyond the tools actually observed in this run.
slice.conflict_check: CLEAN boundary preserved; only public primary sources and cross_field own state/control were consumed. No O, downstream, other-worker semantics, aggregate ledger, or other-role receipts were read.

frontier: OpenTimestamps now has a source-qualified minimal unauthenticated submission contract: raw digest POST to /digest, HTTP 200 binary serialized proof response, no registration/API key in the documented public-calendar path.

The public-calendar contract is documented as free with no account/API-key requirement, so no finite monthly/trial/paid quota is required by that contract and incremental monetary cost is zero; operational rate limits/availability are not proven away.
Submission is at-least-once rather than idempotent: repeated same-digest POSTs can produce distinct proof paths because the aggregator adds a fresh random nonce per submission.
Immediate independent-witness creation remains unresolved only at the scheduled-Chat transport layer: this run did not expose a generic arbitrary HTTPS binary POST capability to the public calendar.
